decisions.executionNote: Establish elbow-up approaches with both grippers open; inspect the new object categories before grasping.
Approach a left white pen and right gold toy car from above, preserving elbow-up posture.
Align gripper jaws across the pen and car, then lower cautiously; table height is estimated from visual geometry.
Use wrist views to refine lateral alignment and approach grasp height for the pen and car.
Center each object between the jaws, close, and make a short test lift to verify retention visually.
Lift the visibly retained pen and gold car clear of the tabletop, then begin moving toward white and blue baskets respectively.
Carry the pen over the white basket and car toward the right side of the blue basket, keeping the arms separated.
Release the pen within the white basket. Replan the car transfer with smaller increments and a lower wrist height after the continuity guard.
Withdraw the open left gripper toward the other white pen. Tilt the right wrist forward while retracting slightly to avoid the IK limit and place the car safely inside blue.
Use much smaller right-wrist recovery increments following the rejected action; left retreats toward the remaining white pen.
Lower toward the second white pen. Shift the car away from the blue basket rim and open the right gripper once over its interior.
Close on the second white pen and make a test lift; withdraw the open right gripper from the blue basket toward the right-hand watch.
Lift and carry the retained white pen toward its basket while positioning the right gripper above the outer watch.
The second white pen slipped back onto the table. Reopen and return for a centered regrasp; cautiously lower the right gripper toward the watch.
Recenter the white pen at its midpoint and align the jaws across its width. Close around the outer watch band at the right.
Adjust the left grasp along the pen toward its center, then close. Test-lift the watch to check whether the band is retained.
Test-lift the recentered pen. The watch was not retained, so reopen and approach its solid case rather than the empty center of the band.
Both objects remained on the table after the lifts. Lower the pen grasp further and align the right fingers around the watch case.
Close at the observed contact height without further downward pressure, then test-lift both objects.
The white pen is now visibly retained. Carry it toward the white basket; reopen and back away from the displaced watch for a clearer view.
Position the held pen fully over the white basket. Approach the displaced watch with a more vertical grasp orientation.
Release the second white pen and withdraw toward the remaining gold car. Correct right-wrist tilt before attempting the watch again.
Both white pens are visible inside their basket. Approach the remaining car with the left arm and the unobstructed central watch with the right.
Make small visual alignment corrections over the car and central watch, maintaining separation between the two grippers.
Close on the centered gold car and test-lift it. Align the right jaws with the watch case rather than the open band center.
Carry the visibly held gold car toward blue. Close the right jaws around the watch's solid case after a small centering adjustment.
Replan the car placement with a small rearward shift and forward gripper tilt to avoid the continuity limit. Test the central watch grasp.
Clear the blue basket rim by retreating and lifting the left wrist. Separate the arms while test-lifting the apparent watch-band grasp.
The watch remains with the right fingers; carry it toward red. The car is outside blue, so reopen the left gripper and approach it again.
Place the retained watch farther inside the red basket. Recenter and close on the gold car outside the blue basket.
Release the watch inside red and withdraw. Clear the blue rim and turn the left fingers vertical before retrying the car.
Approach the car displaced against blue from directly above. Move the right gripper over the remaining watch outside red.
Avoid pressing against the basket rims: test the car grip and retreat upward. Reposition the right wrist outside the red rim before descending.
Reopen and align closer to the objects' centers using wrist images, descending in small increments outside the basket walls.
Shift grasp centers forward to the car body and exposed watch band; close only after a small final descent.
Back away from left rim contact and align the car jaws parallel to the basket edge. Test-lift the right grasp outside the red basket.
Try an inclined car approach with the palm behind the blue rim. Lower the reopened right fingers around the exposed outer watch band.
Reduce the initial left increments after the IK rejection, gradually retreating and tilting while the right approaches the band.
Close around the car after a small inclined descent. Lift and rotate the right jaws to run parallel to the red basket wall, avoiding the earlier rim contact.
Lower the inclined car grasp to its body. With right fingers now parallel to the rim, approach the exposed lower part of the watch.
Test-lift the car away from the blue rim. Close the right gripper around the exposed watch case and band, then lift gently.
Neither test lift retained its object. Reopen, recenter on the displaced car and watch case, and lower the grasp points.
Shift away from the basket walls to center the car body and watch case between the fingertips before closing.
Lift both grasp attempts away from the basket walls and verify retention from the next images.
The gold car is visibly retained. Raise and tilt it forward over the blue rim while lowering the right grasp below the watch case.
The car slipped during wrist rotation; return above it for a stable regrasp without changing orientation while carrying. Close on the watch at the lower contact height and test-lift.
Approach the now-upright car's sides without wrist rotation. Recenter the right grasp on the watch case and descend below the previous missed contact height.
Close on the upright car and the watch case at the observed contact poses, then test-lift without further rotation or downward pressure.
Lower the car grasp below its upper edge. Move the watch band outward from the red wall with the closed right fingertips to make its case accessible.
Bring the car body back between the actual fingertip contact surfaces. Approach the watch's outer band from the clear side, lower and farther from the basket.
Lift the centered car without changing its orientation. Close on the outer watch band and make a vertical retention test.
Carry the retained car high toward the left side of blue without rotating it. Reorient the right grasp to close along the watch case, parallel to the red wall.
Release the car over the blue basket's interior. Approach the remaining watch case with right fingers aligned along the wall rather than across it.
Both cars are now visible inside blue. Withdraw the left arm and remove the right gripper's inward tilt to avoid the red rim during the watch grasp.
Use a slower initial left-arm retreat after the continuity rejection while correcting the right gripper's inward tilt.
Free the right fingers from rim contact by closing and lifting backward. Move the left arm to a clear central staging position.
Approach the remaining black pen with the right arm; stage it centrally for the left arm to place with the white pens.
Lower the right wrist over the black pen midpoint while clearing the left arm for a later central transfer.
Center the black pen shaft between the right fingertips, descend slightly to contact height, and close while the left arm waits clear.
Test-lift the black pen and move toward a central staging point without crossing the arms.
The black pen remained on the table. Return to its shaft with an open gripper and grasp lower than the previous attempt.
Stop descending at the observed contact pose, close around the pen, and make a short vertical retention test.
Carry the retained black pen to the center boundary for a tabletop transfer to the left arm; keep both arms in their own workspaces.
Set the pen down at the center boundary and release. Align the left jaws for a subsequent grasp on its left-side shaft.
Withdraw the right arm into its workspace and approach the staged pen with the left arm from the left side.
Align the left fingers with the staged pen shaft and lower to grasp height. Return the right arm toward the remaining watch.
Make the final left-pen centering correction and close at contact height. Reapproach the watch slowly from above.
Relieve table contact so the left jaws can close around the centered pen. Back the right wrist away from the red rim and tilt for a front-side watch approach.
Carry the black pen toward the white basket with orientation fixed. Try a small front-side watch grasp without further pressing against the rim.
Position the retained pen over the white basket with its full length inside. Test-lift the right grasp clear of the red rim.
Release the black pen fully inside white and withdraw. Insert the closed right fingertips into the watch-band opening to move it away from the obstructing red rim.
White and blue contain their grouped objects. Withdraw the left arm; clear right rim contact and establish a vertical grasp with jaws parallel to the red basket wall.
Return the left arm toward its starting configuration. Use the vertical right-wrist view to align above the watch's solid case.
Clear the red wall by moving the right wrist farther outside, then incline the fingertips toward the exposed band. Finish returning the left arm.
Replan from the interruption with smaller right increments, lowering outside the rim while reaching inward with the fingertips.
The exposed watch band is between the right fingers. Make a small final alignment and close below its upper edge, keeping clear of the red wall.
Lift the apparent band grasp and move slightly outward from the red rim to check retention in a clear view.
The watch case appears retained between the right fingers. Raise it clear of the rim and carry inward without changing wrist orientation.
Move the retained watch completely over the red basket interior, maintaining the successful grasp orientation.
